route: The Plan Got Resized / Bahar-Bistar-Neeche Tak
hook: She wanted bahar. He wanted bistar.
reader_identity_mirror: Couples where one person has outside energy and the other is in rest mode.
emotional_obstacle: Both needs are real: she needs movement, he needs rest.
setup: A normal home scene: bed/blanket, door, shoes, keys, light from outside.
proof: He bargains for 'neeche tak' and appears half-ready, proving he is moving toward her without becoming a perfect outing person.
escalation: The full plan keeps shrinking until it becomes building gate / bench / tiny walk.
bridge: The tenderness is not a moral. It is that neither person had to disappear.
zuv_active_role: He gets up and chooses the smallest real outside.
aachu_active_role: She accepts the smaller plan without turning it into defeat.
send_save_reason: It gives couples a funny phrase for the exact daily negotiation: bahar vs bistar.
silent_storyboard: He is sunk into bed or sofa, blanket up, phone on chest, one sock half-off.
She is ready near the door, not angry, wanting outside.
Shoes and keys enter the scene; he bargains from inside the blanket.
Door opens halfway; her excitement drops for one quiet beat.
He notices, sits up, and reaches for a shoe.
He appears half-ready: one outdoor shoe, one home slipper, still rest-mode.
They step only to the gate, stairs, or nearby bench. She got bahar. He got almost-bistar.
